name: Moonwalk challenge
description: Since astronauts from BubbleCup XI mission finished their mission on the Moon and are big fans of famous singer, they decided to spend some fun time before returning to the Earth and hence created a so called "Moonwalk challenge" game. Teams of astronauts are given the map of craters on the Moon and direct bidirectional paths from some craters to others that are safe for "Moonwalking". Each of those direct paths is colored in one color and there is unique path between each two craters. Goal of the game is to find two craters such that given array of colors appears most times as continuous subarray on the path between those two craters (overlapping appearances should be counted). To help your favorite team win, you should make a program that, given the map, answers the queries of the following type: For two craters and array of colors answer how many times given array appears as continuous subarray on the path from the first crater to the second. Colors are represented as lowercase English alphabet letters.
input_specification: In the first line, integer $$$N$$$ $$$(2 \leq N \leq 10^5)$$$ — number of craters on the Moon. Craters are numerated with numbers $$$1$$$ to $$$N$$$. In next $$$N-1$$$ lines, three values $$$u, v, L$$$ $$$(1 \leq u, v \leq N, L \in \{a, ..., z\})$$$ — denoting that there is a direct path with color $$$L$$$ between craters $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$. Next line contains integer $$$Q$$$ $$$(1 \leq Q \leq 10^5)$$$ — number of queries. Next $$$Q$$$ lines contain three values $$$u, v$$$ $$$(1 \leq u, v \leq N)$$$ and $$$S$$$ $$$(|S| \leq 100)$$$, where $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$ are the two cratersfor which you should find how many times array of colors $$$S$$$ (represented as string) appears on the path from $$$u$$$ to $$$v$$$.
output_specification: For each query output one number that represents number of occurrences of array S on the path from $$$u$$$ to $$$v$$$.
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1045J — Moonwalk challenge [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
